hook.line: Whether you run a café or review one, sooner or later you have to say how good something is. *De calidad…* gives you a measured, grown-up way to do it.
hook.es: Los materiales son de calidad dudosa.
hook.en: The materials are of questionable quality.

examples.es: Los materiales son de calidad dudosa.
examples.en: The materials are of questionable quality.
We offer products of superior quality.

examples.en: The quality of the service has to be improved.

examples.es: Ese café es de muy buena calidad.

examples.es: La tela del vestuario es de mala calidad.
examples.en: The fabric of the costume is poor quality.

rule:
English says a thing "is good quality". Spanish says it is *of* a quality: *es de calidad…*.

Two patterns:
*de calidad* + adjective: *dudosa, media, superior, inferior, deficiente*.
*de* + adjective + *calidad*: *buena, mala, primera, alta, baja*.

The adjective agrees with *calidad*, which is feminine, not with the thing: *un café de calidad dudosa*. Words like *superior* have one form anyway.
To talk about raising standards: *mejorar la calidad*, *garantizar la calidad*.
*Pasable* means barely acceptable. It is not praise.
smallPrint: Teachers call *de* + noun a descriptive complement: it works like an adjective glued onto the noun.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Los materiales son de calidad ___.* (*dudosa* or *dudoso*) The materials are of questionable quality.
yourTurn.answer: Los materiales son de calidad dudosa.
yourTurn.why: The adjective agrees with *calidad*, which is feminine.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Ese café es ___ muy buena calidad.* (*de* or *con*) That coffee is of very good quality.
yourTurn.answer: Ese café es de muy buena calidad.
yourTurn.why: Spanish says something is *de* a quality.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The fabric of the costume is poor quality.
yourTurn.answer: La tela del vestuario es de mala calidad.
yourTurn.why: *De mala calidad* is the plain way to say poor quality.

yourTurn.prompt: Say, as a business: We offer products of superior quality.
yourTurn.why: *Superior* goes after *calidad*, and it has the same form for masculine and feminine.

yourTurn.prompt: Say the opposite: *El jugo es de buena calidad.* (The juice is of poor quality.)
yourTurn.answer: El jugo es de mala calidad.
accept: El jugo es de baja calidad.
yourTurn.why: Swap *buena* for *mala* (or *baja*) and the verdict flips.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *La tela es de calidad media.* (The fabrics are of average quality.)
yourTurn.answer: Las telas son de calidad media.
yourTurn.why: Article, noun and verb go plural, but *calidad* stays singular.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The quality of the service has to be improved.
yourTurn.answer: Hay que mejorar la calidad del servicio.
yourTurn.why: *Hay que* + a verb says what has to be done.

pitfalls.right: Los materiales son de calidad dudosa.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish does not say things "have" a quality here. They *are of* it.

pitfalls.wrong: Los materiales son de calidad dudoso.
pitfalls.right: Los materiales son de calidad dudosa.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Calidad* is feminine, so the adjective ends in *-a*.
Almost. English makes "good quality" a noun phrase; Spanish prefers *de buena calidad*.

personal: Think of something you own and rate it. Say it: *Es de… calidad*.
